title: Tanimoto/Jaccard kernel on binary Morgan fingerprints
notes: k(x,y) = <x,y> / (|x|_1 + |y|_1 - <x,y>), eps=1e-8 on the DENOMINATOR via max(union, eps); see SPEC.md section 1.

Binary 0/1 float32 matmul is EXACT: every partial sum is an integer <= 2048 < 2**24, so no rounding occurs and the Gram matrix is bitwise identical under any BLAS or thread count (verified below by gram_equals_int64_matmul).

On the repo's ACTUAL cached library (data/library/fingerprints.npy, 29678 x 2048 int8, Morgan radius=2): max on-bits = 85, median 47, p99 72. The int8 overflow therefore does NOT currently fire -- it is a latent hazard, not an active corruption. Measured headroom: at radius=3 the max over the 300 widest library fingerprints is 119; at radius=4, 17% exceed 128 and the trap fires; at radius=5, 83% do. The cast is mandatory as defensive engineering, not as a bug fix.

PSD proof recorded here (SPEC.md 1.7): Broder's MinHash gives Pr_pi[h_pi(A) = h_pi(B)] = J(A,B) for nonempty A,B, verified above to within 1.6 MC standard errors. Pr[f(x)=f(y)] for a random f is E_f[<one-hot(f(x)), one-hot(f(y))>], an expectation of inner products, hence PSD. The empty fingerprint is handled by setting its feature vector to 0, which is exactly what eps-on-the-denominator produces (k(0,.) = k(0,0) = 0) and keeps the Gram PSD but singular.

overflow_int16_matmul.description: same with int16: no wrap up to 2048

overflow_int8_matmul.description: (row @ row.T) with dtype int8: wraps modulo 256 into [-128,127] for >= 128 on-bits. THE TRAP.

overflow_intersection_int8.description: Xo @ Xo.T left in int8: wrapped, and the diagonal is NEGATIVE

overflow_kernel_output_cast.description: the same input with the mandatory float32 cast: diagonal exactly 1.0

overflow_kernel_output_uncast.description: the kernel's output with the int8 cast OMITTED: the clip to [0,1] turns every wrapped-negative entry into 0.0, so the DIAGONAL IS 0 instead of 1 and the Gram is not even a similarity matrix. No exception is raised anywhere.

overflow_on_bits.description: number of on-bits in the probe row

overflow_rowsum_int64.description: Xo.sum(axis=-1): numpy PROMOTES int8 sums to int64, so this is correct. Only the matmul wraps -- that asymmetry is what makes the bug silent.

overflow_true_value.description: the mathematically correct <x,x> = number of on-bits

overflow_uint8_matmul.description: same with uint8: wraps at 256 on-bits
